data.narrative:
DiamFab is a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Khaled Driche, Gauthier Chicot, and Ivan Llaurado that has raised €8.7M to date. The target operates within a fragmented Chips & Semiconductors sector where 12 private peers and 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) exist, though no seed-stage peer set met statistical sufficiency for direct median benchmarking.

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using total capital raised (€8.7M / ~$9M) as a proxy for base value, a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to next stage implies a valuation of $22M. Peer-median benchmarking was inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peers within the narrow semiconductor cohort—12 peers exist across the sector, but fewer than three comparable data points survived filtration for stage proximity and valuation tier. Public-comp anchoring using the median 21.0x P/S multiple across the three semiconductor tickers could not be executed absent the target's revenue disclosures, which are standard nondisclosure for private companies.

The analysis supports a range of $18M–$25M, centered on $22M, derived exclusively from stage-progression mechanics. Key uncertainties remain the target's revenue trajectory, capital efficiency relative to frontier-tech peers (Cerebras, SambaNova, PsiQuantum), and execution risk inherent to seed-stage semiconductor ventures. Validation of this range will require either peer fundraise data or revenue-based anchoring as the company progresses.
